page-data-aiSort.text: Let an AI make your categories Categories, rules, tags, display names, card payments and salary, made for your own spending, with any AI chat you already use. The app puts each payment into a category (like Food or Car) so you can see where your money goes. Setting this up by hand, shop by shop, takes a long time. Here an AI chat does it for you: it reads the names of the shops and payers in your transactions and writes rules, so new payments are sorted on their own. Follow the 3 steps below. You check every suggestion before anything is added. Only the names leave the app, never amounts, dates or accounts. 1. Download your transaction texts A file with the 12 different names in your transactions. Download 2. Ask an AI chat Copy the instructions, paste them into an AI chat (for example ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini), and attach the file. Copy instructions 3. Upload the answer The AI first shows you a table to check. When you are happy with it, it gives a file or a block of text. Upload it here to see what it would add. Upload the answer See the instructions I use a money app and want my spending sorted into categories. The attached file lists the names that appear in my transactions (shops and payers), how many times each appears, and whether money went out or came in. It also lists what I already have: categories, tags, display names, card payment texts and salary texts. Don't repeat those. Please work out: 1. categories: 8 to 25 clear categories that fit these transactions. Reuse my existing categories where they fit. Mark categories for money coming in with "income": true. Write the names in English, short and simple. 2. rules: for each name you can sort, a short piece of it (at least 2 letters) that always appears in it and does not appear in unrelated names, and the category it belongs to. One rule can cover many names, for example a chain with many branches. Every category used in a rule must be in your categories list or in mine. 3. tagRules: only if clearly useful, a short piece of a name and one or more tags (a short word, for example a trip or a project). 4. displayNames: only where the bank's text is messy (codes, numbers, cut-off words), a short piece of it and a clean, short name to show instead. 5. cardPayments: texts of bank lines that pay the bill of a credit card company. 6. salary: texts of money coming in that is really salary from an employer. Not other income. Leave out names you are not sure about. I will sort those myself. First, before any file, show me here in the chat a preview table with one row per name: Name, Category, Tags, Display name (empty when the name stays the same). Below it, short lists of the card payment texts and the salary texts you found. Then ask me to confirm or correct it. Only after I confirm, give the result as a downloadable .json file if you can make files, otherwise as one JSON code block. Use exactly this shape: { "categories": [ { "name": "Groceries", "income": false }, { "name": "Salary", "income": true } ], "rules": [ { "contains": "supermarket", "category": "Groceries" } ], "tagRules": [ { "contains": "hotel", "tags": [ "trip" ] } ], "displayNames": [ { "contains": "PAYPAL *SPOTIFY 4029", "name": "Spotify" } ], "cardPayments": [ "isracard" ], "salary": [ "acme ltd" ] } The AI gave text, not a file? Paste its whole answer here Check it

page-data-setCardRules.text: Card payments 1 If a payment from your bank contains the text in the place you choose, it is the bill of a credit card. It is not counted as spending, because each purchase is already counted on the card. If Add rule If → Card payment Delete Recognised automatically, with no rule: Isracard · ישראכרט, Visa Cal · כ.א.ל · ויזה כאל, Max · מקס · מקס איט פי, American Express · אמריקן אקספרס, Diners · דיינרס, Leumi Card · לאומי קארד. Also any bank payment equal to what a card was charged on that day.
